his-b120: People with impaired kidneys do need to be more cautious with high, rapid magnesium dosing, because they may not clear excess magnesium out well. But they should be far more worried about taking the MDMA which depletes it (and shifts other electrolytes dangerously), since MDMA can injure the kidneys even more, not to mention potential muscle breakdown and overheating. However, if they have already taken the MDMA, I'm not saying they should sit there and let the jaw tension get worse. I just wouldn't tell them to copy my gram-per-minute magnesium chloride dosing approach blindly, since that's a higher-risk situation where they should be taken to a hospital ASAP.
a2-b127-b128:
If they swallowed it within the last hour or so (slow-release pills leave a few hours more), activated charcoal may help, since it binds to a lot of drugs in the gut before the body can absorb them. It only helps with what binds to it, which leaves out alcohol and lithium among other things, and it can also adsorb medication they need. I'd only give it to somebody who's fully alert and able to swallow, because anybody who is vomiting, sedated, seizing or otherwise unable to protect their airway could breathe it into their lungs (aspiration).

If you're unsure charcoal would be of any value to them, poison control may be useful. They're also who to ask when you can't tell what the substance is or what it does in combination with something else they took, or when there may be a delayed risk (the worst coming hours later). I don't treat calling poison control as a mandatory ritual, though, since how useful they are varies by country and by whoever answers. And what they give you is help deciding, so go on with any first aid while you talk to them.
a2-b130: Serotonin syndrome can look like some of the emergencies above, since it can also bring on a seizure or dangerous overheating. But the rescue measures in those other branches do not necessarily treat it, so check for it too whenever they've had something that raises serotonin. That includes ayahuasca and other MAOI brews, MDMA, DXM cough syrup and many antidepressants, as well as other MAOIs, the painkiller tramadol, the antibiotic linezolid and some opioids. Too much of any one of them can bring on serotonin syndrome, and so can a medication that was just started or had its dose raised, but I'd suspect it most when two of them were combined.
